title: Maximize Sum Of Array After K Negations
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. One operation picks any index `i` and changes the sign of `nums[i]` (it becomes `-nums[i]`). Perform exactly `k` operations; picking the same index in several operations is allowed. Return the greatest total of `nums` that can remain after all `k` operations.
notes:
## Intuition

Changing the sign of a negative number raises the total by twice its size, so the most negative numbers are the best ones to flip first. Once no negative numbers are left (or no flips are left), any extra flips are a cost. Two flips on the same index cancel, so only the parity of the leftover flips matters: if it is odd, one value must end up negative, and the cheapest choice is the value with the smallest absolute value. A brute force would try every set of indices to leave negated, which is exponential.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order so the most negative values come first.
2. Walk from the front with `i`, negating each negative value while `flipsLeft > 0`.
3. Add up the array into `sum` and track its `smallest` value. If any flips are still left at this point, every negative was already flipped, so all values are non-negative and `smallest` is the cheapest one to negate.
4. If `flipsLeft` is odd, one more flip is unavoidable: subtract `2 * smallest`.
5. Return `sum`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4, 2, 3]`, `k = 1`.

- Sorted: `[2, 3, 4]`. There are no negatives, so `flipsLeft` stays `1`.
- `sum = 9` and `smallest = 2`.
- `flipsLeft` is odd, so `sum = 9 - 2 * 2 = 5`.

The answer is `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the two passes are O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Find `smallest` after the negations: in `[-2, 1]` with `k = 2`, the second flip must go to `1`, not to the original `-2`.
- An even number of leftover flips costs nothing, and neither does any leftover when a `0` is present (`smallest` is `0`).
- Do not loop `k` times flipping one element at a time with a full scan; with `k` and `n` up to 10^4 that is 10^8 steps.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `flipsLeft` | operations not yet used |
| `i` | index of the next value to examine in the sorted array |
| `sum` | total of the array after the negations |
| `smallest` | smallest value after the negations |

narration.2: Sort so the most negative numbers come first.
narration.3: No operation has been used yet.
narration.5: Keep flipping while flips remain and the next value is still negative.
narration.6: Turning a negative into a positive raises the total the most.
narration.13: Visit every value after the negations.
narration.15: Track the smallest value, the cheapest one to negate later.
narration.18: An odd number of leftover flips forces one value to stay negative.
narration.19: Negate the smallest value: it loses twice its size from the total.
